intro: Emerson Ranch is a master-planned subdivision in Oakley, ZIP 94561. City records show design review for its Citrus neighborhood in March 2017. National builders opened further sections in the years after, including a Lennar grand opening in February 2022.
Homes this recent may still be under builder coverage. This page covers the calls that still happen, such as small leaks, outdoor water use, running toilets and water heaters.

sections.h2: Check the builder's warranty before you book a repair
paras: A new-construction home often carries a builder warranty on workmanship and a separate manufacturer warranty on the water heater and fixtures. The terms differ by builder and by year, so read your closing paperwork first. A repair done outside the warranty process can complicate a claim.
If the problem is an active leak, shut off the water first. Then call the builder's warranty line and a plumber on the same day, so nothing floods while the claim is opened.

sections.h2: Where small leaks tend to show up first
paras: These are general places to look in any home. They are not a claim about what is happening in Emerson Ranch.

items.d: Turn everything off and watch the low-flow dial. If it keeps turning, water is escaping somewhere. Our [[leak-detection|leak detection]] page explains how a hidden leak is traced.
A wet patch on a lawn strip or a spigot that drips after it is shut off is an outdoor leak, and it adds to the water bill quietly.
A flapper that does not seal lets water trickle into the bowl all day. A drop of food coloring in the tank shows it in minutes, and [[toilet-repair|toilet repair]] covers the fix.
Supply lines and traps can weep at the connection. Look for damp cabinet floors and mineral crust on the fittings.

sections.h2: What the 20-year sewer rule means for newer homes
paras: The sewer district's camera inspection rule applies only to older properties at the time of sale. Check the year built on your county record. A home under 20 years old may not be covered yet.
It will matter later, and the lateral is the owner's responsibility at any age. Ironhouse Sanitary District can confirm whether a sale triggers the inspection.

faqs.q: Should I call the builder or a plumber for a leak?
a: If the home is under builder warranty, tell the builder, and shut off the water first so the damage does not grow. You can still call a plumber to stop an active leak the same day.

faqs.q: How can I tell if I have a hidden leak?
a: Turn off every fixture and watch the water meter's low-flow indicator. If it moves, water is leaving the system somewhere. Tracing the location is the job of leak detection.

faqs.q: My toilet runs on and off. Is that a plumbing emergency?
a: Not usually. A worn flapper or fill valve is the common cause and it wastes water, so fix it soon. Close the toilet's wall valve if it overflows.

faqs.q: Does the sewer inspection rule apply to my house?
a: The district asks for a certificate on sale of a property more than 20 years old. Check your home's year built and call Ironhouse Sanitary District to confirm.
